subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams file uploads adopt the proposed five-minute base plus 256 KiB/s size budget, with this file-consent PR landing before the overlapping SharePoint-send PR?
rationale: Source, tests, and controlled HTTPS proof establish correctness, but neither Microsoft’s contract nor live-tenant evidence determines OpenClaw’s permanent minimum transfer rate or the preferred landing order for the shared helper.

options.title: Approve and sequence
options.body: Approve the proposed transfer policy, land this narrower consent-upload change first, then rebase the SharePoint-send PR onto the shared helper.

options.title: Consolidate both paths
options.body: Pause this PR and combine the personal-consent and group/channel timeout changes into one owner-reviewed PR with one policy and proof set.

options.title: Require tenant calibration
options.body: Pause both PRs until a real Teams tenant upload demonstrates that the proposed deadline safely covers representative slow transfers.

recommendation.title: Approve and sequence
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed transfer policy, land this narrower consent-upload change first, then rebase the SharePoint-send PR onto the shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is the recent file-consent boundary and test work in commit 347f7b9550064f5f5b33c6e07f64e85b9657b6f1.
